vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: team-dispatch
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle implements a complex multi-agent orchestration system that performs high-risk system modifications, including the installation of background persistence via launchd, systemd, or cron (scripts/watch-install.sh) and the granting of broad agent execution permissions (allowAgents: ['*']) by modifying the global openclaw.json configuration (scripts/setup.sh). While these behaviors are aligned with the stated purpose of managing task timeouts and multi-agent dispatching, the automated setup of background services and the expansion of the agent's privilege boundary represent a significant increase in the host's attack surface.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions broadly match a multi‑agent orchestration purpose, but they ask the agent to perform system-level changes (create symlinks, write global configs, install a persistent watcher, restart the Gateway) while declaring no required binaries or credentials — that mismatch and the persistent background installation are disproportionate and worth manual review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi‑agent orchestration, DAG dispatch, durable tracking) match the included assets: agent templates, project.json, watcher scripts, and many workspace files for subagents. Creating workspaces, copying templates, and wiring subagents into openclaw.json is coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly requires the agent to run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/setup.sh up front and to perform an environment detection phase. The instructions direct creating symlinks, writing ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json and modifying openclaw.json (including setting main.subagents.allowAgents:["*"]), creating agent directories, creating sessions/, rendering and installing a launchd plist / scheduled task, and restarting the Gateway. Those are broad, system‑level actions beyond mere orchestration logic and give the skill the ability to change agent permissions and install persistent services.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal 'install' spec, but many local scripts and assets are packaged with the skill and the SKILL.md instructs running them (setup.sh, watch.sh, publish-clawhub.mjs). This is higher‑risk than an instruction‑only skill because code on disk will be executed locally. There are no downloads from odd external URLs in the provided files; the repo includes a local Node publisher and watcher scripts. Still, the package executes system commands (bash/node/python) but does not declare required binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: requires.env is empty, yet the runtime instructions and config reference external models (openai-codex/gpt-5.x), node scripts, and optional Telegram notification configuration. The skill writes global OpenClaw agent configuration (openclaw.json) and enables broad subagent permissions (allowAgents: ["*"]) — a privileged change that should be explicitly justified. The skill also installs persistent watchers and may invoke networked tools (clawhub publish helper). Declaring zero required binaries/credentials is inconsistent with these behaviors.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill installs persistent artifacts: a symlink into ~/.openclaw/skills, per‑agent workspace files under ~/.openclaw/agents, a launchd plist / Windows scheduled task to run the watcher, and it restarts the Gateway. Although always:false, these modifications create long‑lived changes and increase blast radius (especially because openclaw.json is altered to allow subagents). This combination of persistence + config changes merits manual inspection before enabling the skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be what it claims (a multi‑agent dispatcher) but it performs intrusive, persistent system changes and the SKILL.md forces running its setup script. Before installing: 1) Inspect scripts/setup.sh, scripts/watch.sh, and scripts/publish-clawhub.mjs for commands that call network endpoints (curl/git/ssh/node/npm) or execute subprocesses; 2) Back up ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and any existing agent workspaces; 3) Run setup.sh manually in a controlled environment (VM/container) or with a dry‑run option if available; 4) Verify the script does not add unexpected remote endpoints or collect secrets; 5) Confirm you accept the watcher (background job) and the Gateway restart; 6) If you require least privilege, ask the author to (a) list required binaries and env vars, (b) avoid setting main.subagents.allowAgents to ["*"] by default, and (c) provide an explicit dry-run mode and an uninstall script (uninstall.sh is present — inspect it). If you want me to, I can scan the key scripts (setup.sh, watch.sh, publish-clawhub.mjs) line‑by‑line and summarize exact filesystem and network operations.
